sections.title: More morning actions
sections.content: Beyond zuhanyozom (I shower), a few more -ik verbs cover the rest of getting ready: mosakodom (I wash up), fésülködöm (I comb my hair), borotválkozom (I shave). Brushing your teeth uses a different pattern — fog ("tooth") takes the accusative -t and pairs with the ordinary verb mos ("to wash"): fogat mosok, literally "I wash tooth".

items.english: In the morning I wash up and brush my teeth.

sections.content: mosakodik ends in -kodik, the same frequentative shape you may have noticed on other Hungarian verbs describing something done to or for oneself — you don't need the pattern itself yet, just recognize mosakodom as its own vocabulary item for now.
